**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

The document contains no non-compete or field-of-use restriction binding Northwind. In fact, clause 12.3 affirmatively locks in the playbook's *preferred* position — it confirms nothing restricts us from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, or operating in any field or territory, and records Vendor's acknowledgement that we have made no exclusivity, non-compete, MFC, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.

The only competition covenant runs the other way: clause 12.4 restricts Brightline from developing or marketing a service competing with our analytics products during the term. That benefits us, so per the direction rule it is not flagged. Clause 13.4 (reverse engineering) is standard IP protection, not a business restriction, and clause 24 (no Vendor assignment to a Customer competitor) is likewise protective of us.
